summary.text: The Chicxulub crater is an impact crater about 200 km across, buried beneath the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico.
It formed slightly over 66 million years ago when an asteroid about 10 km wide struck Earth.
The impact's devastation and climate disruption are widely accepted as the main cause of the extinction of 75% of species, including all non-avian dinosaurs.

facts.label: Found by
facts.value: Geophysicists Antonio Camargo and Glen Penfield

items.prompt: Rocks around the world share a thin clay layer rich in iridium, a metal rare on Earth but common in asteroids. How did it most likely get there?

options.label: Erosion piled up Earth's own scarce supply
A nearby exploding star rained it down
A vaporized impactor spread it through the air
Rising seas laid it down along every coast

items.explain: The idea is that the impactor vaporized, its iridium spread into the atmosphere and settled across Earth's surface as an enriched clay layer.

items.prompt: What were the geophysicists who discovered the crater originally searching for?

options.label: Petroleum
Dinosaur fossils
Gold deposits
Fresh groundwater

items.explain: Camargo and Penfield came across it in the late 1970s while looking for petroleum in the Yucatán Peninsula.

items.prompt: Penfield presented his crater evidence at a 1981 conference, yet it drew little attention from impact experts. Why?

options.label: His employer banned him from speaking about it
The talk was given only in Spanish
His slides were lost before the talk
Many of them were at a rival meeting that week

items.explain: The conference was under-attended because many impact and K–Pg experts were at the Snowbird meeting the same week.

items.prompt: Which find in the surrounding rocks helps show that the Chicxulub crater was made by an impact?

options.label: Shocked quartz
Coal seams
Coral reefs
Salt deposits

items.explain: Evidence for its impact origin includes shocked quartz, a gravity anomaly, and tektites in surrounding areas.

items.prompt: Many paleontologists at first rejected the idea that an impact caused the extinction. What was their objection?

options.label: No iridium was found outside Italy
Few fossils near the boundary hinted at a slow die-off
Asteroids were thought too small to matter
The clay layer was much younger than the fossils

items.explain: The lack of fossils close to the K–Pg boundary, the three-meter problem, suggested to them a more gradual die-off.

items.prompt: Why can't visitors to the Yucatán Peninsula see the Chicxulub crater as a giant bowl?

options.label: Thick rainforest hides its rim from view
Wind has worn its walls completely flat
Lava later poured in and filled it up
It lies buried beneath younger rock layers

items.explain: The crater is buried about a kilometer deep beneath younger sedimentary rocks.
